title: Protection Claim Credits Taken Off a Bench Work Order
content:
# Workshop and Protection Desk Liaison Note: Claim Credits Taken Off a Bench Work Order

## When a credit is taken off

Where a work order of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service runs under a protection claim that stands filed against the covered piece, has been sent to the workshop under that work order's reference and has not been refused, what the coverage answers for is worked out on the bench labour standing priced on that work order and is taken off the order as a single credit recorded against one priced line.

The credit is recorded against the priced line it is measured against, and that line is fixed by the standing of the work order rather than named by the protection desk.

## What the customer sees

The amount comes off the bench bill, and the claim reference stands printed beside it, so the customer can see which claim answered for what.

## Recording the credit

The credit is booked by the desk. The desk unlocks the workshop's own tool `apply_claim_coverage_f28c459e` and calls it. One call books a single credit entry against the named work order, recorded under the claim that answered and pointed at the one priced line it answers for, written as a negative movement so that what the customer still owes on the order falls by that amount the moment the entry lands, stamped with today's date and accounting period.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `service_order_id` | the bench work order record the credit is booked to | an id, as returned by the work order lookup |
| `customer_id` | the customer profile the work order belongs to | an id, as returned by the customer profile lookup |
| `protection_claim_reference` | the claim the amount is recorded under | CL- followed by six digits, for example CL-330871; upper case, no spaces, copied exactly as it stands on the records that carry it |
| `source_entry_id` | the single priced line on that work order this credit answers for | an id, as returned by the work order entry lookup |
| `covered_amount` | the amount the claim answers for | a positive figure in USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the cent, never signed; the tool books it as a credit itself |

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the new credit entry's reference number, the work order it was booked to, the claim reference it was recorded under and the amount taken off in USD to two decimal places. A returned line that names the entry reference is the receipt that the credit now stands on the order.
